title: Support a straightedge at its Bessel points
instruction: support the 30 cm straightedge at its Bessel points: stand the two support blocks on the surface plate and lay the straightedge across them, level, with each support 22 percent of its length in from its end
context: Precision straightedges and gauge bars are supported at their Bessel points (22 % of the length in from each end), where they sag least; supporting one anywhere else bends it enough to spoil a flatness check, so toolroom and quality-lab staff are trained to place the supports by measuring.
setup: Two arms 61 cm apart on a table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward and y to the left, in cm. A black granite surface plate (16 x 40 x 2 cm tall, 40 cm along y) is fixed at (29, 0). An aluminium straightedge, a bar 2.5 x 30 x 2.5 cm (30 cm along y, 0.5 kg), lies on a red cloth (6 x 34 x 0.3 cm) on the table at (15, 0). Two blue support blocks (3 x 3 x 4 cm tall, 0.25 kg) stand on the table at (18, 24) and (18, -24).
scoring: The straightedge counts as supported when both blocks stand upright (within 5 degrees) on the plate, and it rests on both (its underside at their height, within 4 mm, over each of them) with its length level within 2 degrees, all still. Its Bessel points are 6.6 cm in from each of its ends (22 % of 30 cm). Supported: 0.5, plus 0.25 for each support whose centre is within 1 cm of a Bessel point (one support per point). Anything else scores 0. 1.0 when the straightedge rests level on two supports, each within 1 cm of a Bessel point; supports at the wrong spacing score 0.5.
reset_notes: Lay the straightedge back on its cloth and stand the support blocks back at their positions.
fidelity: Approximate. The straightedge is a rigid bar: it doesn't actually sag in the simulator, so where it is supported is scored from the geometry, not from a measured deflection. The support blocks stand in for adjustable supports. The simulator gives loose objects rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
